assertion: Six FDIC-insured banks failed between Nov. 14, 2025 and Nov. 14, 2026, according to the FDIC's list of failed banks.
independent_value: FDIC list: Metropolitan Capital (1/30/26), Community B&T West GA (5/1/26), Kentland (7/10/26), Small Business Bank (7/17/26), Tioga-Franklin (8/21/26), Nano Banc (9/25/26); none between 6/27/25 and 1/30/26

assertion: Nano Banc was larger than the other five failures combined, which together held $712,100,000 in assets.
Regulators closed it on Sept. 25, 2026, and Sunwest Bank took over.
independent_value: FDIC list and press release: closed Sept 25, 2026 by California DFPI; Sunwest Bank of Sandy, Utah assumed deposits

assertion: Assets and deposits in the table: Nano Banc $736,172,000 / $685,846,000; West Georgia $305,716,000 / $296,420,000; Metropolitan Capital $261,185,000 / $212,152,000; Small Business Bank $72,947,000 / $68,773,000; Tioga-Franklin $68,444,000 / $66,571,000; Kentland $3,808,000 / $3,656,000, with the closing dates and acquirers shown.
independent_value: FDIC API QBFASSET/QBFDEP match for Metropolitan, West Georgia, Kentland, Small Business Bank; Nano $736M/$686M and Tioga about $68M/$67M per FDIC (via press release and Banking Dive); dates and acquirers match FDIC list. Exact Nano and Tioga dollar digits not seen in a primary table.

assertion: Estimated costs to the insurance fund: Nano Banc $114,000,000; West Georgia $97,284,000; Metropolitan $19,647,000; Small Business Bank $5,671,000; Tioga-Franklin $5,500,000; Kentland $1,194,000.
reason: Nano and Tioga figures are FDIC preliminary estimates, as published.
independent_value: FDIC API COST 97,284 / 19,647 / 5,671 / 1,194 ($K); FDIC releases $114M (Nano) and $5.5M (Tioga)

assertion: Community Bank and Trust - West Georgia carries the largest published insurance fund cost estimate at $97 million, despite ranking second by size.
source_finding: The FDIC announced $114M for Nano Banc on Sept. 25, 2026; the article's own table shows it
inaccuracy: The claim says West Georgia's $97.3M is the largest published figure; the FDIC release says Nano Banc's is $114M, which is $16.7M higher. West Georgia leads only relative to assets (about 32% vs 15.5%).

assertion: The pending cost estimates for Nano Banc and Tioga-Franklin are the next figures to look for on the FDIC's list.
reason: Both are preliminary and the FDIC says they will change as retained assets are sold; the tension with the article's own table is graded in the preceding claim.
independent_value: FDIC (Nano) and Banking Dive citing FDIC (Tioga): estimates expected to change over time
